extracted.intended_audience: journalists, journalism students, researchers, and general readers interested in the Society of Professional Journalists
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia overview of the Society of Professional Journalists (SPJ) describing its mission, history, membership classes, Code of Ethics, chapters, and awards; useful for understanding SPJ standards, award eligibility, and organizational activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote and defend First Amendment guarantees
rubrics_metrics.description: The stated mission of SPJ is to promote and defend the First Amendment guarantees of freedom of speech and freedom of the press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a core organizational mission/standard that guides SPJ's activities (e.g., Legal Defense Fund, Pulliam First Amendment Award).

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage high standards and ethical behavior in journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: The stated mission of SPJ is to encourage high standards and ethical behavior in the practice of journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as a central purpose of the organization; ties directly to SPJ's Code of Ethics (last updated in 2014) which is what the SPJ is best known for.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote and support diversity in journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: The stated mission of SPJ is to promote and support diversity in journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed alongside other mission goals as an explicit organizational standard to guide programs and policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPJ Code of Ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: SPJ has drawn up a Code of Ethics that aims to inspire journalists to adhere to high standards of behavior and decision-making while performing their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced as a primary ethical guideline for journalists; noted as last updated in 2014 and described as what SPJ is best known for. (Full code text not reproduced on this page.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Eugene S. Pulliam First Amendment Award eligibility/criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The award seeks 'to honor a person or persons who have fought to protect and preserve one or more of the rights guaranteed by the First Amendment.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the stated selection criterion for the annual award honoring First Amendment defenders; the page lists recipients by year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kunkel Awards (game journalism recognition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Launched in 2015 in response to concerns from the Gamergate controversy, the Kunkel Awards were for game journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as an award recognizing achievement in video game journalism; the award was folded into the Mark of Excellence Awards in 2020.

rubrics_metrics.name: Green Eyeshade Awards geographic eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Green Eyeshade Awards annually recognize journalists in Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, Mississippi, North Carolina, Puerto Rico, South Carolina, Tennessee, U.S. Virgin Islands, Virginia, and West Virginia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a regional award with explicit geographic eligibility — a criterion for entry/recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sunshine State Awards geographic eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sunshine State Awards are given each year to journalists in Florida, Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a regional award with explicit geographic eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sigma Delta Chi / Sigma Delta Chi Awards / Mark of Excellence Awards (recognize excellence)
rubrics_metrics.description: SPJ administers awards (Sigma Delta Chi Awards / Mark of Excellence Awards) that 'honor excellence in journalism.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General awards criterion: excellence in journalism; specifics of judging criteria are not detailed on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership classes
rubrics_metrics.description: SPJ has three classes of members: undergraduate, professional, and alumni.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership structure is specified by class; the page notes membership counts and decline but does not list detailed eligibility requirements for each class.
